origin.trigger: MT-019 exposed a general test-resource cleanup defect: process-exit cleanup can exhaust one aggregate budget and leave task-owned database scopes behind. The PostgreSQL instances are historical evidence only; current remediation targets real disposable SurrealDB namespace/database scopes from WP017 MT-341.
origin.why_a_new_mt: The defect is owned by tests/knowledge_pg_support.rs and directly belongs to MT-019 test-resource lifecycle, not MT-020 production_factory.rs. The operator requires an unexpected same-WP gap to be retained as a future MT when it does not directly belong to the current MT.

scope.summary: Make real-SurrealDB integration-test namespace/database teardown bounded, exact, and reliably leak-free for the WP-1 process-ledger and real-process lifecycle suites.
scope.root_cause: Sequential cleanup of many task-owned database scopes under one aggregate deadline lets one slow cleanup consume the budget for later scopes. Each disposable SurrealDB namespace/database needs its own bounded cleanup opportunity and independent canonical reread.
forbidden_paths: PostgreSQL or SQLite connection, fixture, migration, fallback, or proof behavior
Broad namespace, database-pattern, or server deletion
Suppressing cleanup failures without a bounded observable receipt
Stopping SurrealDB or any process not started by this MT
acceptance_criteria: AC-1: Cleanup operates only on the exact task-owned namespace/database scopes returned by the WP017 MT-341 SurrealDB test allocator; no wildcard, server-wide, or foreign-scope deletion is permitted.
AC-2: Every allocated SurrealDB namespace/database receives an independent bounded cleanup opportunity, so one slow cleanup cannot consume the cleanup budget for later scopes.
AC-3: Best-effort process-exit cleanup remains non-panicking and observable, while normal per-test cleanup happens early enough that process exit is only a recovery fence.

AC-4: Fresh full process-ledger and real-process lifecycle suites pass against Handshake-managed SurrealDB and an independent official-SDK canonical reread proves zero namespace/database scopes allocated by those runs remain.
AC-5: Failure-path tests prove an individual cleanup timeout/error does not prevent later exact scopes from receiving cleanup attempts and does not target foreign namespaces/databases.
scope.risk_if_missed: Repeated full SurrealDB validation leaks task-owned namespace/database scopes, bloats managed state, slows later tests, and can make otherwise-correct work appear flaky or blocked.

implementation_notes: Preserve the cleanup intent, not the historical PostgreSQL mechanism: use the WP017 MT-341 real-SurrealDB exact-scope allocator and official SDK.
Prefer normal-scope RAII or explicit teardown; retain process-exit cleanup only as a bounded recovery fence.
Direct every Cargo target to Handshake_Artifacts and clean it after proof.
red_team: A single larger timeout preserves the aggregate-budget bug and will regress as rollouts grow; the budget must be per exact namespace/database scope or cleanup must occur earlier.
Dropping every similarly named scope could delete a parallel agent's live SurrealDB namespace/database; exact allocator ownership and foreign-scope survival are mandatory.
A green test binary does not prove cleanup; canonical SurrealDB state must be reread independently after process exit.

v6_owned_files_basis_2026_09_06.note: Lane-owned teardown target and the shared embedded test-store support module it extends. Cargo.toml carries this MT's additive [[test]] declaration but is SHARED across every lane per [KB-CARGO-SHARED-001], so it is not listed as owned.
v6_owned_files_basis_2026_09_06.shared_file_policy: Files every lane compiles (Cargo.toml, lib.rs, any mod.rs, storage/surreal/schema.*, the shared test-support module, and the ModelLane provider) are SHARED under [KB-CARGO-SHARED-001]. Edits to them invalidate every lane's build cache, so they are queued and landed in one pass at a lane-quiet boundary, and every live lane is told what changed.
